newsitem.title: USA: Pacific Exchange to change stock price quotes - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Pacific Exchange to change stock price quotes - WSJ.

text.p: The Pacific Exchange could submit a rule change to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission as early as today to start quoting stock prices in sixteenths of a dollar, the Wall Street Journal said in Monday's electronic edition.

While almost all of the regional U.S. stock exchanges have said they are considering such a move, the New York Stock Exchange has so far resisted lowering its one-eighth minimum increment for most stocks, the newspaper said.

"Boston, Chicago and the Pacific exchanges have all talked to me about asking how they can begin to trade and quote in sixteenths," Richard Lindsey, director of market regulation for the SEC, was quoted as saying.
Dan Carlson, vice president of corporate affairs for the Pacific Exchange, was quoted by the Journal as saying it might not start trading in sixteenths immediately.
